name: IM-1

target.name: Odysseus landing site near Malapert A

surface_window.note: From landing (February 22, 2024) to end of mission (seven days after landing), as published.

outcome_note: Landed February 22, 2024 near Malapert A. The six NASA instruments ceased operations seven days after landing, meeting pre-launch projected mission operations.

payloads.name: Lunar Node 1 Navigation Demonstrator
payloads.purpose: Navigation beacon demonstrating autonomous positioning with radio ranging signals.

payloads.name: Stereo Cameras for Lunar Plume-Surface Studies
payloads.purpose: Stereo cameras imaging the descent-engine plume's effect on the surface.

payloads.name: Radio-wave Observations at the Lunar Surface of the photoElectron Sheath
payloads.purpose: Low-frequency radio receiver measuring the near-surface photoelectron sheath.

payloads.name: Navigation Doppler Lidar for Precise Velocity and Range Sensing
payloads.purpose: Lidar measuring velocity and altitude during descent to touchdown.

payloads.name: Radio Frequency Mass Gauge
payloads.purpose: Gauges propellant quantity in low gravity.

payloads.name: Laser Retroreflector Array
payloads.purpose: Passive retroreflectors serving as a precise location marker.

sources.title: Intuitive Machines IM-1 On The Moon! (LROC, 26 February 2024)

notes: Landing and end of mission are known to the day, not the hour.

site.name: Odysseus landing site near Malapert A
site.source_note: The coordinate where the lander came to rest, as published; used as given, not searched. Height and slope sampled from the 80 m LOLA model at the nearest post.

notes: Mission facts are compiled by hand from NASA pages, LROC images and the IAU Gazetteer; every record carries its sources, last read 2026-09-27.
1 of 1 missions have fields no source confirms; they are listed as unconfirmed, never filled in.
Numbers are Sun and Earth geometry at the target over the mission's surface window, not what any lander measured.
